key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within hours. Acute, dramatic presentation. LOCATION: Diffuse, PERIUMBILICAL. Not localized to one quadrant. DURATION: CONSTANT from onset. Pain persists continuously without relief. CHARACTER: SEVERE, CONSTANT pain initially crampy/colicky, then becomes steady. Described as deep, severe ache. AGGRAVATING: Eating may worsen (post-prandial angina pattern). Movement doesn't significantly change (pain internal). RELIEVING: NOTHING helps. Pain is UNRELENTING despite narcotics. Requires vascular intervention for relief. TIMING: CONSTANT and unrelenting. No wave pattern. Progressively worsens. SEVERITY: 9-10/10, PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION to exam findings (severe pain but minimal tenderness on exam - hallmark). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: BLOODY DIARRHEA (late finding), nausea, vomiting, urgent bowel movements. Patient in severe distress despite soft abdomen. KEY POSITIVES: Classic triad: severe pain + minimal exam findings + elderly (>60) with vascular disease (AFib, PVD, prior myocardial infarction ). Metabolic acidosis. KEY NEGATIVES: Young patient WITHOUT vascular disease makes extremely unlikely. Severe tenderness on exam suggests alternative.

red_flags: EMERGENCY CONDITION - severe pain out of proportion to exam in elderly with AFib - call 911 immediately
Bloody diarrhea with severe pain - bowel infarction, needs immediate vascular surgery
Peritoneal signs developing - bowel necrosis/perforation, fatal without emergency surgery
Metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate - tissue ischemia, extremely poor prognosis without immediate intervention
